claims.statement: The document declares the fields id, group, baseline, outcome and delivers six data rows containing two group values.
One observation, labelled "b" in group A with baseline 12 and outcome 15, is delivered twice as byte-identical rows.
Two rows carry an empty field: "d,B,,14" lacks a baseline and "e,B,13," lacks an outcome.

Consequently the delivered row count (6), the complete-pair row count (4) and the count of distinct complete-pair observations (3) are three different numbers, and any summary must name which one it uses.
The document records no allocation mechanism, so it cannot be read as describing a randomized comparison and no design label may be attached to it.
